items.followUp: How many bits are there in 3 bytes?

rubric.why: Identifies the number of bits in one byte.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a byte has 8 bits.
Award 1 mark for clearly relating one byte to 8 bits.

rubric.why: Shows that ciphertext is produced by encrypting plaintext.
rubric.description: Defines ciphertext as encrypted plaintext or a message.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying ciphertext as the encrypted form of a message.

rubric.why: Explains its unreadable or coded nature, or that decryption is needed to recover the message.
rubric.description: States that ciphertext is coded/unreadable without decryption.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the original message must be decrypted to be understood.

modelAnswer: Ciphertext is the encrypted form of a message (plaintext).
It is coded and cannot normally be understood until it is decrypted.

items.followUp: State two ways to protect data from unauthorized access.

rubric.why: States the basic purpose of data security.
rubric.description: Data security protects data from unauthorized access.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that security prevents unauthorized people from accessing data.

rubric.why: Gives another risk that data security helps prevent.
rubric.description: Security also helps protect data from misuse, alteration, damage, loss or theft.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning at least one additional threat to data.

modelAnswer: Data security is necessary to protect data from access by unauthorized people.
It also helps prevent data from being misused, altered, damaged or lost.

items.followUp: What is one advantage of sharing files over a network?

rubric.why: Captures the basic meaning of file sharing.
rubric.description: File sharing makes files available to other users.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that files can be shared or made available to others.

rubric.why: Identifies who or what can exchange the files.
rubric.description: Files are exchanged among users or computers, commonly over a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning other users/computers or a network.

modelAnswer: File sharing is the process of making files available to other users or computers.
It commonly allows users to exchange files over a network.

items.followUp: What does a web browser use HTTP to communicate with?

rubric.why: Identifies the full name or abbreviation of HTTP.
rubric.description: HTTP stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly expanding HTTP or giving its abbreviation.

rubric.why: Explains HTTP's role in transferring web content between a browser and a web server.
rubric.description: HTTP is a set of rules used to transfer web pages or other web data between a browser and a server.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its use in transferring web content or communication between browser and server.

modelAnswer: HTTP stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol.
It is a set of rules used to transfer web pages between a web browser and a web server.

items.followUp: Name the two main devices that communicate in a basic communication system.

rubric.why: States the main purpose of a communication system.
rubric.description: A communication system enables the exchange or transmission of information/data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it sends, receives or exchanges information or data.

rubric.why: Identifies that communication takes place between communicating parties or devices.
rubric.description: Information is communicated between a sender and a receiver, or between devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the sender/receiver or equivalent endpoints.

modelAnswer: A communication system is used to send and receive information or data.
It carries information from a sender to a receiver.

items.followUp: Name any two common network topologies.

rubric.why: Defines topology as the arrangement or layout of network devices.
rubric.description: Network topology is the arrangement or layout of devices in a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining topology as the arrangement/layout of network devices or nodes.

rubric.why: Recognizes that topology also describes how devices are connected.
rubric.description: It describes the connections among network devices, physically or logically.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning network connections or physical/logical layout.

modelAnswer: Network topology is the arrangement or layout of the devices (nodes) in a network.
It shows how the devices are connected, physically or logically.

items.followUp: What does HTML use to mark the structure of a web page?

rubric.why: Explains hypertext as text containing links to other documents or locations.
rubric.description: Hypertext is text that includes links to other text, pages or documents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying hypertext as linked text.

rubric.why: Explains that a markup language uses tags to describe a document's structure or presentation.
rubric.description: A markup language uses tags to mark or define the structure/presentation of a document.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the role of markup language or its tags.

modelAnswer: Hypertext is text that contains links to other text or documents.
A markup language uses tags to define the structure or presentation of a document; HTML is a markup language.
